headline: Waymo, Alphabet's driverless taxi company, has increased its first private loan to $5 billion.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 2: the report is from 6 Oct (before the window) and the terms come from people familiar with the deal.
importance_line: What changed: the robotaxi company is borrowing more to fund its fleet and new cities, which matters to the riders in those cities and to the investors taking the risk; the doubt: the terms are second-hand, the loan has not formally closed, and the companies did not comment.
summary: Bloomberg reported on 6 Oct 2026 that Waymo had increased its first private debt deal to $5 billion, up from the more than $3 billion it first sought, and Transport Topics carried the story on 7 Oct. The loan is allocated and expected to close soon, with the bond investor Pimco, the private equity firm Blackstone and Sixth Street Partners among the investors.
notes: Text read on Transport Topics (ttnews.com), which carries the Bloomberg report; Bloomberg itself returned a bot check. Re-dated (event 6 Oct): Full Report rule 4.1 holds re-dated items back; the QA step decides.
